items.question_text: Explain why squares, equilateral triangles and regular hexagons can each tile the whole plane.
items.reason: The example is the angle arithmetic at a corner (4 x 90 = 6 x 60 = 3 x 120 = 360) and gives no figure; the three tilings are already the teaching image of this concept, which is not linked.
items.text_alternative: Keep the five steps as text and LaTeX: $4 \times 90^\circ = 360^\circ$, $6 \times 60^\circ = 360^\circ$, $3 \times 120^\circ = 360^\circ$.
